newsitem.title: USA: Calif. cuts SDG&E revenue $33 mln/yr, SoCal Gas up.
newsitem.headline: Calif. cuts SDG&E revenue $33 mln/yr, SoCal Gas up.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) said Friday it reduced the amount of operating costs which will be recovered in natural gas rates by Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co, while slightly raising the cost recovery amount for Pacific Enterprises' Southern California Gas Co.
The new rates will be in effect until July 31, 1999.
The CPUC allows the utilities to change commodity natural gas rates monthly depending on gas prices.
SDG&E's annual operating revenue requirement was decreased by $33.07 million to $1.129 billion, the CPUC said.
The changes are expected to reduce SDG&E's residential customer gas rates by 2.7 percent.
SoCal Gas annual revenues will be increased by $1.6 million to $2.607 billion.
The CPUC noted SoCal Gas will collect from customers "stranded" costs resulting from an agreement to give up capacity rights on the El Paso and Transwestern gas pipelines.
The changes are not expected to significantly affect SoCal Gas residential customer rates.
